item.title: SCP Idea - Lost World
item.description: My idea for SCP and tale it tells.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article + Tale

Genre (Optional): Emotional

Page Layout (Optional): Containment, Description, Exploration and Tale connected to it.

Elevator Pitch: Mansion in which pianist remains is placed 2 miles East in Allegheny National Forest. Anomalous pianist creates world and story of it's fall in his music. People that will hear his music hallucinate through it's whole story being able to hear and see everything, but not being able to interact with that world. People under influence will feel like the story continues for hours while in normal time it's only about 5 minutes long. After seeing it's whole story, influenced individuals show symptoms of extreme depression and inability to die of old age as they are "already dead inside".

Central Narrative: Everything occurs in mansion build 2 miles East in Allegheny National Forest. SCP Foundation got intel about this SCP, through many suicides happening lately in the forest. Previously mentioned anomalous pianist plays a song with length of 4 minutes and 56 seconds, but for influenced person it's like hours. Pianist shows them all tragedies of "lost world". Everyone who sees the story became extremely depressed and unable to talk about it to the point where influenced individuals commit suicide. People influenced by this SCP are empty. They are alive, but they barely eat, drink or sleep and a they do is look nowhere. People that saw the story are unable to die of old age as they are "already dead inside". Only one D-Class individual was able to keep part of his sanity and as ex writer, he was able to write just a portion of what he saw as a tale. D-Class few weeks after dies by stabbing his own throat with pen, he was given to write the rest of story.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I waned to focus on emotional pressure on reader and I just waned to write what and how I feel.

Additional Notes:
I didn't wrote what the story contains for purpose to keep it hidden for now.
I has about it's story, but it's not overall important just as it's core.

item.title: The Petrifying Statue
item.description: A statue which only attacks humans and human shaped beings, killing them by petrifying their internal organs and fluids.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror

Page Layout: Traditional structure of containment procedures followed by description.

Elevator Pitch:

  • This is a statue crafted by AWCY and placed in a public place.
  • When no humans are stood close to it, it remains a statue but when a human is stood close to it, they will be attacked.
  • If they cannot escape, they are killed by an unknown process which petrifies their internal organs and fluids.
  • Humans can avoid the attack by breaking up their human form with exterior objects and costumes.

Central Narrative: It is a traditional article, which is further expanding the anomalous object count which the group is responsible for.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A statue which requires humans to be present for its anomalous properties to manifest, but this manifestation can be worked around by various means, protecting said person from a horrible death where their insides are solidified.

item.title: Blood Storm
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional):

Page Layout (Optional):

Elevator Pitch: A storm that appears once every 4 years in a completely random location on Earth. The rain is red and feels like blood and if touched with bare skin it will turn you into a mindless zombie with increased speed and strength. It is not possible to convert people back to normal.

Central Narrative: This SCP is usually the size of the state of Texas. It will appear on a random day after 4 years in a random location at a random time which makes it much harder to tell if the storm is abroad. The first hour of the storm will appear as just cloudy but after the hour is over, the rain will begin to pour. During the first hour, civilians in the range of the storm will be warned of the storm via EAS on television, radio, and cell phone. Anyone not taking cover will be detained by arriving MTF agents. Aggression towards MTF agents will be met with lethal force. The storm will usually last between 16 to 28 hours and once its over, all civilians in the area must be given amnestics to forget about the past hours of the storm. Anyone lost during the event must be given a cover story as to why they are gone.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: During the most recent event, a man created a journal explaining his experience of the storm and everything that happens while the MTF guard the streets to keep people safe.

Additional Notes: I would like suggestions of how to make this better if it isn't too good.

item.title: (SEEKING GREENLIGHT) This Number is no Longer in Service
item.description: A disconnected phone used by a desperate man
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Drama/Emotional

Page Layout: I plan to use the traditional SCP format with an ACS header. The plot will reveal itself through the recovery log and a set of phone calls received by the object.

+ show block
– hide block

Elevator Pitch: In the 1968 the Foundation incepted a package from one of their mailrooms. The package contained a 1940’s rotary dial telephone that receives a phone call every day at 12:00 AM despite the cord being cut. The same phone call is repeated nightly until it is changed by the caller. The phone calls slowly reveal the story of a foundation researcher who has been captured by the Chaos Insurgency. He intended to send the phone to his family in hopes to ensure them that he is safe.

Central Narrative: The calls the man makes to his family slowly reveal a story. In the first call he will inform his family that “the guys at work” have a job for him and that he won’t be home for a little while. In the second phone call the man is less optimistic, however his tone is still hopeful and he attempts to ensure his wife that he will be home soon. He refers to his captures as “they”. In the final phone calls he refers to his captures as the Insurgency (Chaos Insurgency) and is mostly pessimistic in tone. In the final phone call, he apologizes to his family and is ill. These phone calls will take place over the course of 50 years.

An addendum at the end of the article will state that the foundation visited the home address that the man sent the package to. House was empty and it is implied that the family living there was killed by the Chaos Insurgency. This is meant to get an emotional response out of the reader. Not only were his calls not received by his family, but rather the foundation, but his family may not have been alive this entire time.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This article will stand out because of its extremely simple concept that requires emotional investment. It is easy for any reader to understand (you do not even need to know what the Chaos Insurgency is to understand the basic premise). It is meant to be a refreshing break from the more complex articles on the site.

Additional Notes: The following information will be given during the article:
1. No phone calls can be made on the phone. It functions as a normal, disconnected phone when not receiving its nightly call.
2. The object is classified as neutralized, as it no longer makes calls.

item.title: The Knife (SEEKING GREENLIGHT)
item.description: An anomalous knife which surprisingly was contained by the Foundation.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Mystery

Elevator Pitch: It's a kitchen knife with coordinates on it leading to a small island which doesn't seem to have any anomalous activity. If anyone lays an eye on the knife, without a camera or artist depiction, they will hear whispers of voices telling them to 'become one with him'. The Foundation currently does not know what this phrase means. Anyways, the victim will have an urge to equip the knife to once again 'become one with him'. The victim will chant 'I must become one with him' and once said victim holds up the knife, the victim is now considered a 'host'. The host will be controlled by some unknown entity and is severely hostile to humans. After host manages to catch an unfortunate being, it will ingest the victim before falling dead and the knife will dematerialize and then materialize in a random location. Witnesses who manage to get a glimpse of the host will suddenly suffer cardiac arrest due to unknown means. Cameras or artist depictions do not trigger the knife's affects.

Central Narrative: Several reports came through on an evening saying that multiple civilians have mysteriously gone 'insane' and a another bunch have somehow created a cult around a specific kitchen knife worshipping it. Then other reports came in reporting that multiple civilians in a town began acting strange and soon enough the entire town was in anarchy. Eventually, the Foundation found out about this strange event and so 'invaded' the town, securing it and the knife with the loss of 7 agents in the process. The remaining agents all suddenly chanted 'This world will fall into anarchy' after the mission.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: It includes a mysterious 'him' which could make the reader figure out who this 'him' was and why the cult was created along with why the chanting occurs.

Additional Notes: First attempt at making my own SCP sooo.. yeah it probably won't be that good but eh

item.title: Feedbacker/Infinite Repeater
item.description: Boss DD3 pedal that will repeat/feedback infinitely, and will get into your head too.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror, Black Comedy

Page Layout: Basic Entry w/ interview logs

Elevator Pitch: Stoner musician buys a Delay pedal from UK antique shop and weirdness ensues.

Central Narrative: Jason Higgs purchases a cheap BOSS DD-3 delay pedal from his local antiques shop (town of Rye, Sussex, UK). He takes it home and maxes out all the pedals' settings. Upon turning off his amplifier, he is surprised to find the sound of the feedback loop continuing.

He disconnects the power, but the loop continues still and his panic gradually intensifies. He attemps to destroy the item, but when attempting to do so he is struck with what he later describes as a stroke. He awakens minutes later and finds the item still perfectly intact. He throws it into a bush in panic, and begins pacing toward the hospital. He begins hearing the same feedback loop in his head, although faintly.

He arrives at the hospital and is eventually transfered to another hospitals' psych ward following his manic behaviour. The staff of both hospitals found nothing medically wrong with him, and found no quantifiable evidence of his condition.

2 weeks later, he tells the doctors that the loop has "syncronised" with his heartbeat, and that it has gradually grown louder and lowered in pitch. It is at this point he learns he is being held at an SCP site in Kent. He is interviewed orally (albeit unsuccesfully as his hearing is nearly completely inhibited) then via text communication.

Another week later, he claims the loop has gotten so low in pitch that it's like an earthquake. He begs to die, and eventually is terminated.

During these events, the foundation recover the item. They test the item on several D-Class, who all respond similarly to Jason although with slight variations depending on mental fortitude. It seems to take around 5-7 days from first hearing it for the loop to "enter" the subjects' mind.

They attempt to break into the item using many implements and methods but with no success.

The item has a way of nulifying any violent force applied to it, and shows only slight superficial stratches when dropped from great heights or launched long distances. It is also extremely heat resistant, and is not corroded by strong acids. It is then contained in a glass display case in a 3mx3mx3m room, and classified as "Safe".

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Mysterious item with strange anomalous "effect", largely unexplained

Additional Notes: Interview logs will flesh item backstory out more

item.title: The Sanctum
item.description: A prison below of Vatican, where an ancient order contains its own anomalies to protect the world but is uncovered by the foundation.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: No

Page Type: GoI format/Potential for separate SCP article on the prison and the Star of Bethlehem.

Genre (Optional): History, Horror, Action

Page Layout (Optional): Standard SCP article. Numerous addendums and field reports/logs as the foundation push deeper into the prison.

Elevator Pitch: Numerous SCPs undocumented by the foundation is located in the most unlikely place, The Vatican City. Beneath the city lies a 300-meter deep prison protected by powerful Templars, and priests known as Arminda's. The ancient prison contains SCPs via 'blessings' granted by the 'Star of Bethlehem' a large light orb at the top of the prison, which in itself is it's own SCP.

Central Narrative: The story begins when foundation agents in Italy begin to vanish, and once found are clueless on their allegiance to the foundation, appearing to not remember the foundation at all. The investigation leads the foundation to the Vatican City, with numerous unknown agents responsible for the agent's state being linked to there.

+ Further Narrative
- Title for hiding text

To understand the cause of this, the foundation sent in an infiltration unit into the Vatican to watch for bizarre activity, having a live feed and wiretaps attached to them. Upon entering, the squad found nothing out of the ordinary, until they witnessed a singular man in white robes wall through a large display waterfall and vanish. The foundation now had proof that anomalous activity was occurring within the Vatican, and would have surely been able to uncover more there and then if the squad had returned…

Concerned for a potential hostile threat, the SCP foundation conducted a full investigation into the activity. Including a squad sent to contain the white-robed priest- but yet again the squad failed to return, no bodies, no trace. Eventually, the foundation launched a full raid on the Vatican, and what they would uncover was The Sanctum, the Vatican's very own version of the SCP Foundation, home to over 300 undocumented SCPs. In the center was a large pit traveling down 300 meters, and above was a bright ball of light that appeared to light the whole prison.

Upon entering, the foundation made contact with those who ran this facility. Ancient knights known as the Templars, and white-robed priests known as Armindas. When met, a man in a golden robe told the strike team "Welcome to The Sanctum, but this is no place for you." Attempting to force entry brought hostility, and a fight broke out between the strike team and The Templars, who despite wielding only armor, swords, and shields, were able to dispatch enough foundation units to force a retreat. From this point, The Sanctum is declared an enemy of The Foundation, and a full platoon of mobile task for units are sent in to claim the facility, but they fail, the mysterious orb of light beginning to vaporize the units as they descend to the bottom.

The story continues as the foundation attempts to decide whether to take the Sanctum by force or attempt to negotiate and uncover the true power of the orb of light what the Sanctum call 'The Star of Bethlehem' and why and how they contain anomalies. But most importantly, what lurks at the very bottom of the prison. (There is a bit more to fit in but I didn't want to cram this article, but if you wish to hear more do ask!)

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I believe the idea has a lot of potentials to introduce new things the foundation never knew existed and uncover the true power that the Sanctum holds, and how it and the Foundation tetters on war or peace with each other. And the secret of what lies at the bottom of the prison, along with finding out how and why the Sanctum does such things.

Additional Notes: N/A

item.title: Foundation 2.0
item.description: How far do you go to keep the foundation alive, if its all that it means to you?
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Tragedy, Emotional, Comedy

Page Layout (Optional): A brief description and containment measures describing a parallel dimension which can be reached by some obscure ritual, and a village inside it, but story mainly told by a journal found by the foundation when they found out how to get inside. The foundation eventually leaves the dimension and doesn't return due to little reason to explore as the people and objects appear somewhat similar and they see no reason to take unnecessary risks.

Elevator Pitch: A foundation guard gets stuck in an alien dimension via contact with 507 when trying to break to break up a fight with a d class attacking them for some reason / the result of addemdum 507 - 00, and ends up in a parallel dimension with a village and villagers, that are similar to humans, but slightly behaviourally and physically different with a different language, and cause humans to disassociate from reality if continually touched

Central Narrative: The foundation later finds an obscure way into the dimension, and finds a journal and ruins of his base detailing his life. The agent steals from the villagers, and spies on them, trying to make proper files and dossiers on them, even making his own scp site, but eventually devolves into a cariacature of the foundation, capturing non - anomalous animals the he beleives are to study and make files on, as well as making overprecise and downright incorrect assumptions about the villagers in needless documents about their lives. He also tags the walls and trees with scp signs, and writes incoherent notes in his journal pertaining to enemies of the foundation and scps. He then breaks his leg and slowly dies because of sepsis, and reflects on what he did, and feels happy he contributed to the foundation.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: How the guard loses his mind and becomes so obesessed with the foundation he forgets what it stands for and what it actually does, contain anomalies, and save humanity.

Additional Notes: I would like the journal to be somewhat comedic (eg: "gamers against weed are dumb little kids", "the goc is for nerds"), and make useless files on completely normal animals,
(e.g:
object class: keter
description: a rabbit i found, is anomalous but i dont know how yet
containment: a cage next to my bed
tests: eats carrots and shits occasionally), but I don't know if it would be funny enough/too meta/too much content

I'm new to this, so please correct me if anything stands out as off or out of place.

item.title: Seeking Greenlight - Man in the Mirror
item.description: Maybe it's egotism, maybe it's real, maybe it's maybelline.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: The SCP refers to a hypothetical anomaly. A new "Foundation," which operates extraordinarily similarly to ours, almost the exact same but for a few differences, which has been clearly operating for years upon years, has suddenly come to our knowledge. Surely, the only way they've been existing for so long without us knowing is if they were using an anomaly to hide themselves… right? Surely, no one matches the Foundation in their ability to hide themselves from the rest of the world…

Right?

Central Narrative: The narrative is going to follow the first encounter between our SCP Foundation, and the PCS Foundation (Process, Condemn, Shield), and then followed up by a MTF exploration of a PCS facility in hunting for the SCP, then recounting an exact replica of the events that occurred at the PCS facility, except it's an interview recounting the exact same events occurring at a SCP facility. By the end, no actual SCP is recovered, or even hinted at existing, hopefully leaving the reader asking if it's possible that just maybe two foundations were so good at hiding that up until now, they hid from each other.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I know theoretical/non-existent SCPs have been done before, but I'm hoping the description here is enough of a hook to keep things going.

Additional Notes: I know I'm not the greatest at summarizations. It may need some.. work. I'd be happy to clarify anything if the need should be there. Additionally, I sort of jumped the gun and wrote up an unfinished draft. If anyone would like, I'd be happy to let you read it, although it needs some heavy revising.

item.title: "Intro to Thaumaturgy" College Textbook
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Comedy

Page Layout: An initial standard page going over the published editions of the book. Then a log of incomplete, poorly copied extracts of the text without magic - supposedly due to low quality. Followed by an up-to-date article documenting a edited copy of the tome, with a log of the different corrections made by a disenfranchised pupil. Containment procedures allow for the book to be borrowed by approved request.

Elevator Pitch: A secondhand university thaumaturgy textbook which is defunct and a scam, but is still listed as required reading. It has been corrected by an angry ex-student to make it functional.

+ Show whatever
- Hide whatever

Central Narrative: The book is drawn to the foundation's attention when it is incredulously found via web-crawlers on online marketplaces. It is quickly scrubbed from the website due to Foundation concerns about secrecy. A team of researchers are tasked with tracking down copies of the book. However all that can be found of the book are monochrome, poorly reproduced photocopies. These extracts prove to be useless in assisting thaumaturgical practices.

They receive a package containing the book from a disgruntled student. This leads the foundation to discover it is a textbook for a specific professor who charges $25,000 USD or "a year's servitude to dark forces" for it. The book is covered in angry notes expressing frustration in the inaccuracies of it such as " What am I supposed to use?? Pig's blood or wolf?" and "There's no godsdamn way that is an acceptable salt circle…". The amount of corrections and further notes fix the rituals and magic to work as intended. The Foundation reclassifies the published versions as non-anomalous and classifies the only anomalous version to be the corrected one.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The thaumaturgy methods and descriptions in an academic way and the premise that not even magic prevents you from being screwed over by the educational system.

Additional Notes: Would appreciate idea on how the actual corrected book is anomalous and not just containing data that can be used to create anomalies, and any areas of thaumaturgy on the SCP universe I should try and include in the photocopy example extracts?

item.title: A Photo Book of Murderers
item.description: My third attempt at SCPs again. Need critique and if worthy greenlight.
item.content:encoded:
Idea Post:

Seeking Greenlights: Primarily Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror a lot, Drama/Emotional a good deal, History a little.

Page Layout (Optional): Basic special containment procedures and description followed by how it was obtained, then testing logs, and finally incident reports (maybe). I also want to provide a record of an MTF who has been trapped in the book.

Elevator Pitch: Photobook slash journal used by a former researcher working at an asylum (the early ’50s to ’70s) studying primarily murderous and violent patients. People who place a photo in the book begin to have their memories and their personalities overwritten with psychotic patients.

Central Narrative: I want to highlight the malpractices and the sickening practices of asylums that studied the brains of ‘psychotic’ individuals. Reports of weird experiments have always been rumored and very few reports survive from these places because some of these acts were perpetrated by leading scientists who used this research to better our understanding of psychology. There are even reports of human sacrifices and brutal use of pagan rituals and some real dark sh. Whether or not these are real stories says what if they were really basically. Anyone who places their photo into the book will be able to have their own personality imprinted on another person, however, these people claim they have been taken to an asylum far away from where they were brutally experimented on. Those who went in perfectly sound in mind frequently return with broken minds. There is an eighty percent chance that within the first hour if the person whose photo is removed their personality will stop being overwritten however for every hour it decreases by twenty percent. And for every hour less and less of the subject's sanity is retained.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: What is unique in my opinion are the stories the imprinted patients can tell to people, the horrors they experienced, and how it happened.

Additional Notes: I know there are no factual claims to the horrors of such asylums in real life but I just want to tell the story, please don’t come to tell me why it isn't factual. It's SCP it ain’t meant to be factual it's meant to be fun!

At the exact same moment, four exact copies of that person or those people, linked through physical experience, are generated in four random places on the planet, with one of them in mortal peril and the rest left to experience the death as an introduction to their new, linked experience.

+ show block

The Foundation experiments with the SCP, first confirming it's safety as well as confirming the sanity and normality of the copies before making a small team of operators, three copies of the same agent, using the SCP after it's experimentation shows it's safe status. That status is revoked when the second person sent through, a higher level operator specializing in Keter Class wet work, becomes the 'sole survivor.' Rather than experiencing a coming together of support and love of his other copies after grieving together, creating a unit far more capable than most, the Sole Survivor experiences their death three times and has a mental breakdown, joining the Chaos.

item.title: SCP - The Infinite Quarter
item.description: A simple 25¢ coin that can multiply
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP-#### “The Infinite Quarter” is a 2019 San Antonio Mission Texas Quarter with the head side scratched out with a unknown instrument. The quarter seems like an average coin but when left unobserved the coin will start to rapidly multiply until observed or all open space is occupied. All other instances of the scp do not share the same anomalous duplication ability as the main coin and will only share the ability of ceasing duplication when the coins are observed though if one were to observe a duplicated instance of the coin and not the original coin it will not stop the original from duplicating.

Central Narrative: The coin would of first been discovered when foundation agents caught wind of a man who seemed to of out of the blue came into a fortune oddly enough in quarters. Upon investigating and obvious administration of amnestic, they discovered a shoe box completely full of quarters. It wasn’t until the agent investigating the box looked away and then back to discover that the box had begun to overflow with quarters before stopping. After finding the anomalous coin they brought it to the foundation and contain it in a specially made plastic case big enough to fit a single quarter.

** Hook/Attention-Grabber:** All duplicated instances of the coin will be in perfect condition and not sharing any of the scratch marks on the head side of the coin like the original does. I had also thought to make it so that the actual original coin is always the easiest to spot as to make it more easier to be observed to warrant its duplication stopping when viewed.

** Additional notes:** possible idea is the scp foundation will sometimes use this scp for possible funding for resources and the like.

item.title: SCP Idea
item.description: Th Arkansas Creek Walker, A.K.A. Mosquito Mass.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article.

Genre: Horror.

Elevator Pitch: A strange, humanoid mass of vampiric insects has been tormenting parts of America.

Central Narrative: Wild animal population has been decreasing rapidly as of late in the Southwest part of America, as well as hunters. Something strange is happening, and farmers in the area have seen it in front row seats.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The bugs are mosquitoes. Not any normal mosquitoes, though. They are omnivorous, and will dig through any biological material to get some meat. This means it will eat through wood, dirt, and any other greens, but not stone-like substances.

Additional Notes: I just want to know if there should be anything that could possibly be leading the entity other than just being a paranormal happenstance.

item.title: The Jukebug
item.description: What if that song you got stuck in your head stayed there?
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes
Page Type: SCP Article
Genre: Horror
Page Format: I plan to use the standard page format, adding in interviews and audio logs to tell the stories of three separate cases.

Elevator Pitch: An auditory cognitohazard that latches onto the brain waves of a person until the afflicted person hears a “catchy" song. Once the afflicted has a song stuck in their head, the anomaly perverts the lyrics to encourage the afflicted to act out intrusive thoughts. The anomaly can lie dormant for up to three days without a song to embed itself into, before eventually dissipating. The anomaly can be detected through basic brain activity scans, appearing in the shape of an insect on images of the brain. If a song is introduced that the afflicted finds catchy, the anomaly will stay undetected by the afflicted for two more days. During which it will play the song excessively in their mind. Anytime the afflicted sings the song, their brainwaves are modified to transmit the anomaly into the minds of others, starting a separate cycle. After the two day infection period, the anomaly begins to goad the original afflicted. The more the afflicted resists, the harder it pushes with symptoms ranging in severity. The Foundation can eradicate the anomalous brain activity by playing music that lacks (in the opinion of the listener) pleasant rhythm or rhyme, for 18 hours.

It is unclear if this anomaly is merely a phenomenon or an entity. No evidence of an entity occupying the physical body of any afflicted people exist, other than vivid descriptions of a singing insect-like creature seen during the REM cycles of the afflicted, in the first several days of exposure. The vivid and consistent descriptions of this creature, coupled with the insect-shaped brain image, have lead to a dichotomy in the observing staff. Those who believe it is merely a phenomenon, which the evidence seems to support the most, have developed the current SCP protocols. A separate team, continues to search for evidence of what they call the “Jukebug.”
Central Narrative: Multiple accounts of different instances of the “Jukebug,” including: the aftermath of a child's birthday party, a surgeon, and a musician working on their newest song.

Hook: I think the idea that you could have been infected by this SCP and it’s already too late is spine-chilling and compelling enough to draw people in.

Additional Notes: Since the anomaly spreads due to divergent brainwaves of a person during the recitation of the song in their mind I am not sure if this is actually an auditory cognitohazard or not.
